llm_details.reasoning: There is no bounds check verifying that crgram_len does not exceed sizeof(sbuf) - 1 before performing memcpy(sbuf + 1, crgram, crgram_len).

The target buffer `out` has capacity `outlen`. `len` is clamped by `len = (apdu.resplen > outlen) ? outlen : apdu.resplen;`, ensuring `len <= outlen`. Since `offset >= 0` and `offset < len` (or 0), the copied size `len - offset` is at most `len <= outlen`, so `memcpy(out, apdu.resp + offset, len - offset)` cannot overflow `out`.

In `tcos_select_file`, `memcpy(path, in_path->value, in_path->len)` copies `in_path->len` bytes into `pathbuf` (which has fixed size `SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE`). There is no check verifying that `in_path->len <= sizeof(pathbuf)` prior to the `memcpy` call.

The memcpy copies `sizeof(*serial)` (56 bytes) from `&card->serialnr` to `serial`. Both `serial` (type `sc_serial_number_t *`) and `&card->serialnr` (type `sc_serial_number_t`) have a fixed compile-time size of `sizeof(sc_serial_number_t)`, so copying `sizeof(*serial)` bytes between these two valid structures cannot overflow the source buffer.

The memcpy copies `sizeof(*serial)` bytes from `&card->serialnr` to `serial`. Both `serial` and `&card->serialnr` are of type `sc_serial_number_t` (size 56 bytes), so reading 56 bytes from `&card->serialnr` is an exact-size struct copy from a valid, fixed-size structure buffer within `card`.

In `tcos_decipher`, `crgram_len` is user-controlled/caller-provided and not checked against the size of `sbuf` (`SC_MAX_APDU_BUFFER_SIZE`, typically 261 or similar fixed APDU size). If `crgram_len + 1 > sizeof(sbuf)`, `memcpy(sbuf+1, crgram, crgram_len)` causes a stack buffer overflow.

The destination buffer `pathbuf` has size `SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE` (which is standardly 16 bytes in OpenSC, matching `sizeof(in_path->value)` where `sc_path_t.value` is an array of size `SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE` and `len` cannot exceed `sizeof(value)` per OpenSC path invariant / struct definition `u8 value[SC_MAX_PATH_SIZE]`). Copying `in_path->len` bytes from `in_path->value` to `pathbuf` does not overflow.

Both `serial` and `&card->serialnr` are pointers to structures of type `sc_serial_number_t`. Copying `sizeof(*serial)` (56 bytes) from `&card->serialnr` to `serial` is a standard struct copy and does not exceed the bounds of either object.

Both `serial` and `&card->serialnr` are pointers to structures of type `sc_serial_number_t`. The copy length is `sizeof(*serial)`, which matches the exact allocation size of `sc_serial_number_t` (56 bytes), so neither the source nor destination buffers are accessed out of bounds.

When copying `key_obj.label` via `memcpy(key_obj.label, info_blob + offs + 2, len);`, the code clamps `len` to `sizeof(key_obj.label) - 1`, but fails to check whether `offs + 2 + len <= info_len`. If `info_len` is smaller than `offs + 2 + len`, reading from `info_blob + offs + 2` will read out of bounds.

The memcpy copying into `kinfo.id.value` with length `len` from `info_blob + offs + 2` is preceded by explicit bounds checks: `offs + 2 > info_len`, `len + offs + 2 > info_len`, and `len > sizeof(kinfo.id.value)`. Both the source buffer and destination buffer boundaries are fully validated prior to the call.
The function checks `if (!buff || len < 0x24)` before the memcpy, which guarantees `buff` has at least 0x24 (36) bytes available, safely covering the 0x20 (32) byte copy.

The for loop condition specifically checks `offs + 2 + 2+2+2 + 2+2+2 + 2+36 <= len`. Since `ptr` begins at `buff + offs + 2`, and is advanced by 6 * 2 = 12 bytes, `ptr + 2` is at `buff + offs + 2 + 12 + 2 = buff + offs + 16`. Reading 36 bytes accesses up to `buff + offs + 16 + 36 = buff + offs + 52`. The loop check ensures `offs + 2 + 6 + 6 + 2 + 36 <= len`, which equals `offs + 52 <= len`. Thus, the loop condition guards the 36-byte memcpy.

Both memcpy operations in sc_pkcs15emu_oberthur_add_cert are guarded against buffer overflows. The source access is guarded by `if (len + offs + 2 > info_len)` and the destination buffer is guarded by clamping (`len = sizeof(cobj.label) - 1`) for the label, or by an explicit check (`len > sizeof(cinfo.id.value)`) for the ID.

The function checks that `buff` is not NULL and `len >= 0x24` before invoking `memcpy(label, buff, 0x20)`. Since `0x20` (32 bytes) is strictly less than `0x24` (36 bytes) and `label` has a capacity of `0x21` (33 bytes), the read does not exceed the bounds of `buff`.

The loop condition explicitly checks `offs + 2 + 2+2+2 + 2+2+2 + 2+36 <= len`, which equals `offs + 52 <= len`. At the memcpy call, `ptr` has been advanced by 2 * 6 = 12 bytes from `buff + offs + 2`, so `ptr + 2` is `buff + offs + 2 + 12 + 2 = buff + offs + 16`. Reading 36 bytes accesses up to `buff + offs + 16 + 36 = buff + offs + 52`, which is within `len` as verified by the loop condition.

There is no bounds check validating that outlen does not exceed the allocated capacity of outbuf prior to the memset call (in fact, octets_left is used uninitialized before memset, and no buffer capacity guard exists).
The loop in `sc_copy_asn1_entry` relies solely on the sentinel check `src->name != NULL` without any bounds or capacity check covering the memory accessed at `*src` (or written to `*dest`).

The function checks that buf and buflen are valid (`if (!buf || !buflen) ...`), and the caller provides `buflen` as the size of the destination buffer `buf`. `memset(buf, 0, buflen)` sets exactly `buflen` bytes of `buf`.

The function sc_asn1_decode_utf8string checks `if (inlen+1 > *outlen) return SC_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;` immediately before calling `memcpy(out, inbuf, inlen);`, ensuring that the destination buffer `out` has at least `inlen + 1` bytes available.

The operation in asn1_encode_path is structure copying `sc_path_t tpath = *path;` (which compiles to memcpy of size sizeof(sc_path_t) == 64). The src-ptr is `path`, which is a pointer parameter to a valid typed struct `sc_path_t`, and dereferencing/copying sizeof(sc_path_t) bytes from a valid struct pointer `const sc_path_t *path` is fully bounded by the struct definition itself.
There is no bounds check or validation verifying the accessibility or bounds of obj->p15_obj prior to the structure dereference/copy (size 2776).

The function checks buffer sizes beforehand and uses outlen explicitly to clear the output buffer (`memset(outbuf, 0, outlen)`). Furthermore, `outbuf` and `outlen` are passed in by the caller designating the allocated buffer capacity. There is no out-of-bounds write from `memset` itself since it only clears the specified capacity `outlen`.

The function sc_copy_asn1_entry copies an array of struct sc_asn1_entry terminated by a NULL name field (*dest = *src, where sizeof(struct sc_asn1_entry) is 40 bytes, compiled as memcpy). In OpenSC, ASN.1 entry templates are standard static sentinel-terminated arrays defined in code. There is no triggerable out-of-bounds bug in the structure copy logic itself.

The function memset(buf, 0, buflen) writes buflen bytes to buf, which is the buffer provided by the caller along with its allocated size buflen. The subsequent bounds checks ensure r_len and s_len do not exceed halflen (buflen / 2), preventing any out-of-bounds access.

In `sc_asn1_decode_utf8string`, the buffer size is verified beforehand with `if (inlen + 1 > *outlen) return SC_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;`. Therefore, `out` is guaranteed to have enough space for both `memcpy(out, inbuf, inlen)` and the trailing null terminator.

The flagged memcpy with size 64 corresponds to the struct copy assignment `sc_path_t tpath = *path;` in `asn1_encode_path`. The pointer `path` points to a valid `sc_path_t` structure, so copying `sizeof(sc_path_t)` bytes is safe and not an out-of-bounds read.

The operation copying `*obj->p15_obj` into a local `struct sc_pkcs15_object p15_obj` (approx 2776 bytes) performs a structure assignment from a validly referenced `obj->p15_obj` pointer. It is not an out-of-bounds access.
